reviewer.tool: agent image read tool on the captured PNGs listed below; numeric Debug draw-state/material records, channel readback and the T29 Clay report

observations: The controlled clay-review identity row renders four authored materials (metal+coat+sheen, emissive+specular, normal-mapped, neutral) as the same neutral gray with no authored chroma and no washed-out white.
The MASK sheet keeps its modelled texture-alpha hole in Clay: the hole reveals the backdrop while the surrounding sheet remains gray. The hole is not filled by the neutral material.

The BLEND/transmissive sheet over the cyan sphere is solid gray in Clay and hides the interior geometry; in Studio the same view shows the sphere through the sheet. No interior mesh leaks through the overridden glass.
Overlapping authored-alpha sheets and the OPAQUE transmissive panel show no tint or blend-order seam in Clay; they are uniform gray and depth-resolve to the nearest surface.
Three small curved parts and the mirrored instance keep readable silhouettes and curved shading; neither clips to a flat white blob nor disappears.
The OBJ line/point control keeps its line and point primitives visible in Clay; the mode round-trip restores Studio pixels and the same pick id.
lighting-probe and sphere-grid in Clay show all material families as one matte gray with soft form and stable exposure; dark and light parts remain ordered.
The STL box keeps hard edges and planar faces; base/lid/cartridge keep cavities and thin-plate silhouettes without washed-out whites.

Car Clay shows solid gray windows with no coloured glass banding, no blend-order seam and no visible interior through the windshield/side glass. The small white speckles along the windshield/roof edges also appear in the Studio capture; they are the pre-existing authored speckle, not a Clay blend seam.
Camera Clay keeps body, lens ring, lens recess and base/strap separation. Microscope Clay keeps brass/enamel part separation and dark cavities. The STEP assembly keeps its two-part separation.
No per-asset-name or per-material-name exception is present in the renderer or the lane.

defects.label: known-defect
defects.where: Car windshield/roof/window edges in both Studio and Clay
defects.description: Small bright speckles along authored window/trim seams are visible in both modes. They are not introduced or caused by the Clay override, but they remain an authored-geometry/edge-quality defect.

defects.label: limitation
defects.description: Clay suppresses authored ORM occlusion with the rest of the material decoration. Cavity/contact darkening will come from the geometry-derived T31/T32 interfaces; T29 deliberately does not use authored AO to hide depth defects.

defects.label: known-defect
defects.description: The external microscope can still report a terminal generation deadline after visible geometry. The T29 run loaded it completely; a future late failure stays a non-passing observation.

positives: Clay rewrites the effective draw bucket on the CPU: BLEND and transmissive triangles join an opaque, depth-writing overlay bucket; the authored Blend PSO and OIT pass are not used.
MASK cutouts are sampled independently of gray shading, so foliage/geometric holes survive the material override.
The neutral matte suppresses colour, metallic, clearcoat, sheen, emission, transmission, specular and normal maps while preserving geometric normals, hard edges and double-sided orientation.
The Studio->Clay->Directional->Studio round-trip leaves vertices, triangles, materials, texture residency, camera, exposure and picking unchanged.
The controlled fixture and the Car/Camera/microscope/base/lid/cartridge/STEP crops give form-readability evidence rather than PBR texture similarity.

acceptance.note: The controlled fixture owns the numeric verdicts; external crops are reviewed qualitatively. Pre-existing Car window speckle is recorded as a known defect, not attributed to this task.
